Habibur Rahman (Md) and others -------- Petitioners
vs
Government of Bangladesh and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Ashfaqul Islam, J: This Rule under adjudication, at the instance of the petitioners, issued on 28-3-2018, was in the following terms: 
"Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon fhe respondent No. 1 to show cause as to why publication of the Gazette Notification dated 23-9-1986 published in the Bangla-desh Gazette by the respondent No. 1 enlisting the House No. NE (O) 5, Road No. 90, Gulshan Model Town, Dhaka-1212 as abandoned property in 'Ka' list at serial No. 53 (Annexure-`A') shall not be declared to have been published without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and show cause as to why inaction of the respondent No. 2 in giving mutation of the property of the petitioners as prayed for (Annexure-M) shall not be declared illegal and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper." 

2. Admittedly, the land in question to wit, situated in the Gulshan Model Town in the Sub-registry office the then District Dacca, Mouja Bhola Samair, Police Station the then Tejgaon being plot No. 5 of Block No. NE(O) standing on 1 (one) Bigha, 4 (four) katha, 6 (six) Chattak thereabouts originally belonged to the then Dacca Improvement Trust (DIT), at present Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakkha (RAJUK) was leased out in favour of one Mr Habib Ansari vide lease No. 109 dated 29-12-1961 by the said DIT for a period of 99 years (Annexure-'B'). 

3. Mr Habib Ansari availed loan of an amount of Taka 1,30,007 by mortgaging the said property from Janata Bank, Motijheel Branch, Dhaka. Since, he defaulted to pay of the outstanding loan, Janata Bank filed Money Suit No. 1077 of 1975 in the Court of 3rd Sub-ordinate Judge, Dhaka and the suit was decreed on 31-8-1976. Janata Bank put the decree into execution in Money Execution case No. 47 of 1976. The suit property was attached and on 3-3-1977 the order of sale of the said property was published in the Daily `Dainik Bangla' and came to the knowledge of the petitioner No. 1 and predecessors of the other petitioners and thereafter the petitioners purchased the said property in auction being the highest bidder at Taka 6,25,000 on 19-4-1977. Sale of the property was confirmed by the Court issuing Sale certificate on 22-8-1977 (Annexure-'C'). 

4. It has been stated that the petitioners having been possessing the said property filed Title Suit No. 564 of 1978 before the then Sub-ordinate Judge, Court No.1, Dhaka on 14-11-1978 against, Secretary, Ministry of Public Works and Urban Development and others for permanent injunction on the property in question. The said Suit was decreed ex-parte on 21-6-1979 in favour of the petitioners. Right thereafter, the petitioners duly mutated the land in question in their names and accordingly different Khatians were published in their names and since then they have been paying rent to the concern Tahshil Office, holding Taxes to Dhaka North City Corporation and so on. 

5. On 3-3-2018, when the petitioners went to the respondent No. 3, Assistant Commissioner of Land, Gulshan Circle, Gulshan, Dhaka-1212, they came to know that the said property was listed in the 'Ka' list by Gazette notification dated 23-9-1986 and for that reason respondent No. 3, Assistant Commissioner of Land, Gulshan Circle, Gulshan, Dhaka regretted to receive rent from the petitioners. It is at this stage the petitioners moved this Division and obtained the present Rule as aforesaid. 

6. Mr ABM Altaf Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing with Mr Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate and Mr Md Shariful Haque, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners after placing the petition and other materials on record mainly submits that no notice was served upon the petitioner No. 1 and their predecessors and the impugned Gazette dated 23-8-1986 (Annexure-'A') was issued without lawful authority having no legal effect. It has curtailing effect on Article 42 of the Constitution. 

7. Next he submits that the petitioners as auction purchaser duly purchased the property in question and the sale of the property was confirmed be executing registered sale certificate which carries with it a legal presumption of genuineness and therefore, the government cannot question and annul the validity of such title by an executive order by gazette notification dated 23-9-1986 which is not tenable in law having no legal basis. It is their submissions that they have been enjoining peaceful possession of the property by paying rent to the government, holding taxes of the Dhaka North City Corporation and also utilizing gas line, electricity line by paying bills and, as such, the gazette notification by the respondent No. 1 passed in utter disregard of the admitted position, which should be treated unlawful and is of no legal effect. 

8. The writ petition has been contested by the respondent No. 1, the Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Works by filing affidavit-in-opposition and also by the added respondent No. 4, the Janata Bank who has also filed affidavit-in-opposition.

9. Mr Sukumar Biswas, the learned Advocate appearing with Mr Kazi Mynul Islam, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, Mr Nasim Islam, Assistant Attorney-General and Mr Nazrul Islam Khandaker, Assistant Attorney-General for the respondent No. 1 by filing the said affidavit-in-opposition has made an elaborate submissions on the issue under adjudication. Firstly, he submits that the then Dacca Improvement Trust (DIT) now Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakkha (RAJUK) leased out the property in favour of non-bengali Mr Habib Ansari vide lease deed No. 109 dated 29-12-1961 for a period of 99 years and accordingly the possession was handed over to him, but the petitioners did not produce the original lease deed and that the petitioners being the auction purchaser having been stepped into the shoes of their predecessor original lessee, Mr Habib Ansari are not immuned from discharging the onus as regards presence of their the predecessor, Ansari during the liberation war. 

10. It has been submitted that the present claimants-writ-petitioners being the auction purchaser have been possessing the case property since 1978 through Court on the basis of a void deed as an unauthorized possessor having no legal right to property in question since the original Lessee Habib Ansari, a non-bengali left the case property uncared at the material time and, as such, the case property itself having had assumed the character of abandoned property under Article 2(1) of the President's Order No. 16 of 1972 had been rightly vested in the Government under Article 4 of the President's Order No. 16 of 1972 and the Government published the same in the official Gazette on 23-9-1986 as 'ka' list of the Abandoned Buildings. It is therefore, the conclusive proof of fact that the said property is an abandoned property under section 5(2) of the Ordinance No. LIV of 1985. 

11. His bone of contention is that the present claimants-writ-petitioners as auction 
purchaser have been possessing the case property since 1978 through Court without any legal right in the said property since the original lessee Habib Ansari left the case property uncared at the material time and as a result the said property itself had assumed the character of abandoned property under Article 2(1) of the President Order No. 16 of 1972 and vested in the Government. 

12. In elaborating his submissions the learned Advocate Mr Sukumar Biswas further submits that under the provisions of section 5(1)(A) of the Ordinance 54 of 1985 inclusion of the property in the list so published is a conclusive proof of fact that the property is an abandoned one and in terms of section 5(2) of the said Ordinance the same has been rightly vested in the Government with effect from 28-2-1972 under the Provision of Article 4 of the President's Order No. 16 of 1972 and therefore, the petitioners status is similar to that of their predecessor Habib Ansari. They hopelessly failed to rebut the said legal presumption of law and facts by producing positive evidences regarding whereabouts and possession of the original lessee Habib Ansari showing payment of rent, WASA bills, electricity bills, telephone bills since 26-3-1971 to 28-2-1972 (relevant time), full payment certificate of RAJUK, domicile certificate which was issued by the District Magistrate, Dhaka under the provisions of Pakistan Citizenship Act, 1951 and relevant voter-list dated 30-1-1973 and 7-12-1976 respectively which were given to Habib Ansari hence, the gazette notification dated 23-9-1986 that included the property in the 'Ka' list remained unrebutted. 

13. It is his further submissions that the law mandates that the claimant of the property has to discharge the onus of proving that the property is not an abandoned property and it is absolutely a stringent burden and the government has no obligation either to deny the facts as alleged by the claimant nor to disclose the basis of treating the property as abandoned property merely because the same is disputed by the claimant. And the claimants in this writ petition, who are the auction purchaser hopelessly failed to rebut the presumption of the conclusiveness of listing the case property in the Gazette Notification. The learned counsel has relied on several decisions in support of his contention which has been stated in paragraph 26 of the affidavit-in-opposition. 

14. Be it mentioned that the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners has also filed several decisions in support of his contention. 

15. We have heard the learned Advocates and the learned Deputy Attorney-General, Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the parties at length and considered their submissions. We have also perused the petition, affidavit-in-opposition and other materials on record meticulously. 

16. At the very outset we want to record that at our instance as we felt it necessary for ends of justice to add Janata Bank as respondent we passed necessary order and added Janata Bank as respondent No. 4. 

17. It is absolutely incumbent upon the claimant who claims the property to be illegally included in the gazette to prove the said property not to be abandoned. First of all we simply failed to understand why Janata Bank was not made a party in the instant writ petition. However, subsequently at our direction Janata Banks was added as respondent in this writ petition. The fact of proving that the property is not an abandoned one and not vested in the Government is totally on the person who challenges the same to be not an abandoned property and intends to take such property out of the list of the abandoned property published in the official Gazette or for any other relief as detailed in section 7 of the Ordinance 54 of 1985. In the case of the Government of Bangladesh vs Md Jalil and others reported in 48 DLR (AD) 10 it was held: 
"The High Court Division, in our opinion, stated with a wrong premise holding that the presumption of correctness of the entries in the Gazette notification does not absolve the Government from denying the facts alleged by the claimant or from disclosing the basis of treating the property as abandoned property when it is disputed. Section 5(2) of the Ordinance clearly provides that the list published under sub-section (1) shall be conclusive evidence of the fact that the buildings included therein are abandoned property and have vested in the Government as such. Section 7 says that a person claiming any right or interest in any such building may make an application to the court of Settlement for exclusion of the building from such list, etc. on the ground that the building is not an abandoned building and has not vested in the Government under President's Order No. 16 of 1972 or that his right or interest in the building has not been affected by the provisions of that Order. The onus, therefore, is squarely on the claimant of the building to prove that the building is not an abandoned property. The Government has no obligation either to deny the facts alleged by the claimant or to disclose the basis of treating the property as abandoned property merely because the same is disputed by the claimant." 

18. The stringent provisions of law that the onus lies upon the claimant of the building to prove that the building is not an abandoned property have been settled by plethoras of decisions. 

19. Now the core question is whether the petitioners are able to prove before this Court that their predecessor Habib Ansari to whom the property had been leased out was present at the relevant time, that is March 1971 to February 1972. 

20. Mr ABM Altaf Hossain, the learned counsel for the petitioners on this score has strenuously tried to impress upon us that the petitioner being auction purchaser was not in a position or in other words he was not required to prove the presence of Habib Ansari for the purpose of proving that the property was not an abandoned property. But it is our considered view that the petitioners are not absolved from the burden of proving to the hilt the whereabouts of Mr Habib Ansari during the relevant period as hinted above. Almost in a similar facts and circumstances our Appellate Division came down heavily in the case of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Public Works Department and Urban Development vs Md Suruzzamal and others reported in 48 DLR (AD) 1. In paragraph 19 of the said reference it has been observed: 
"This Division has held in the case of Gannyson vs Sonali Bank, 36 DLR (AD) 146, that once a property vests in the Government under President's Order No. 16 of 1972 no legal proceedings can be taken against such property. The money decree obtained by Rupali Bank against Dr. Shamim, the execution thereof and the auction sale of the suit property are all void and will not divest the Government of its title to the suit property and the auction-purchaser has acquired no title to the same by his auction purchase." 

21. Facts and circumstances of the above case are almost similar to that of the .case in hand. Admittedly, the property is listed in the 'Ka' list. Therefore, non service of notice upon the petitioners is of no avail. In the case of Rawsanara vs Bangladesh 59 DLR (AD) 165 it has been held that if the property has assumed the character of abandoned property, the listing of the property is perfect, even if without service of notice as per provision Ordinance No. 54 of 1985. It is not material since the property because of non service notice of listing in the 'Ka' list of abandoned property would not loose the character of abandoned property" 

22. This proposition of law has been endorsed by a subsequent decision of Shahidul Haque Bhuiyan and others vs Chairman, 1st Court of Settlement and another 69 DLR (AD) 241. As we have already mentioned that for ends of justice Janata Bank was added as respondent No. 4. By filing affidavit-in-opposition for the respondent No. 4, the learned Counsel Mr Mohiduddin Yousuf, has drawn our notice to paragraph 12 of the same wherein it has been stated that it appears from Annexure-'C' and 'D' to the writ petition that the suit property was auction sold to the writ petitioner No. 1 and the predecessors of other writ petitioners by an order of Subordinate-judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Execution Case No. 47 of 1976 filed by respondent No. 4 for the purpose of executing decree passed in Money Suit No. 1077 of 1975. However, it is a matter of great regret to find that the respondent No. 4 holds no record at all about the said loan account concerned either with the Branch or with Head Office. The loan account concerned is more than 30 (thirty) years old which is treated as past and closed loan account and when the digitalization process of the Bank started around year 2010, all past and closed accounts were left out of the conversion process. It is further stated that the Bank generally holds documents and records of past and closed accounts for no more than 12(twelve) years. Therefore, the quires of this Division whether the original lessee Mr Habib Ansari was made defendant in Money Suit No. 1077 of 1975 and Execution Case No. 47 of 1976; or whether he appeared in the suit; or whether the suit property was mortgaged with the Bank; or whether he was residing in Bangladesh at the relevant time were left unanswered since respondent No. 4, bank had no knowledge in this regard and Bank holds no record as such with it. However, the respondent Bank craves sincere apology in not being of any help to this Division. 

23. Article 2 of the PO 16 in clear terms has spelt out the definition of abandoned property which is as under:— 
"(i) "abandoned property means any property owned by any person who is not present in Bangladesh or whose where-abouts are not known or who has ceased to occupy, supervise or manage in person his property, including-
(i)	any property owned by any person who is a citizen of a State which at any time after the 25th day of March, 1971, was at war with or engaged in military operations against the People's Republic of Bangladesh; 
(ii)	any property taken over under the Bangladesh (Taking Over of Control and  Management of Industrial and Commercial  Concerns) Order, 1972 (Acting President's Order No. 1 of 1972), but does not include-(a) any property the owner of which is residing outside Bangladesh for any purpose which, in the opinion of the Government, is not prejudicial to the interest of Bangladesh; 
(b) any property which is in the possession or under the control of the Government under any law for the time being in force." 

24. Therefore, the irresistible inference which follows that in any course of event the boundened duty to be discharged by the claimant for taking out a property from the clutch of 'abandoned property' has been time and again decided in one line. Though it will be repetition but still we want to reiterate that it is the claimant who shall have to prove to the hilt that the property in question is not an abandoned property. In the instant case the petitioner could not prove that his predecessor Habib Ansari was present at the relevant time as required under law and interpreted by several decisions as discussed above. 

25. That being the situation, we hold that in all fairness this Rule should be discharged. 

26. In the result, the Rule is discharged, however, without any order as to cost. 

Communicate at once. 

End.

Azizur Rahman ------- Pre-emptor-Respondent-Petitioner
Vs.
Mollika Bibi ------ Co-Pre-emptor-Appellant-Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Md. Rezaul Hasan, J.
1. Both these Civil Revision Nos. 3553 of 2007 and Civil Revision No. 3553 of 2007 have been filed by the petitioner against the same opposite parties, on similar contentions. Issues to be decided in these Rules are substantially similar and the common questions of law and facts are involved in both these matters. Hence, these matters have been taken up together for disposal by a single judgment.

2. Rules has been issued in Civil Revision No. 3554 of 2007, calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-5, to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 29-3-2007, passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet, in Miscellaneous Appeal (Pre-emption) No. 47 of 2003 (Heard analogously with Miscellaneous Appeal No. 43 of 2003), dismissing the appeal and thereby reversing the judgment and order dated 20-2-2003, passed by the Assistant Judge, Jointapur, Sylhet, in Miscellaneous (Pre-emption) Case No. 12 of 1999, partly allowing the miscellaneous case should not be set-aside and in Civil Revision No. 3553 of 2007, Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-5, to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 29-3-2007, passed by the Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet, in Miscellaneous Appeal (Pre-emption) No. 43 of 2003 (Heard analogously with Miscellaneous Appeal No. 47 of 2003), dismissing the appeal and thereby setting aside the judgment and order dated 20-2-2003, passed by the Assistant Judge, Jointapur, Sylhet, in Miscellaneous (Preemption) Case No. 12 of 1999, should not be set-aside and/or pass such other order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

3. Facts, relevant for disposal of both these the Rules, in brief, are that, the present petitioner Azizur Rahman filed Miscellaneous (pre-emption) Case No. 12 of 1999, under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, before the court of Assistant Judge, Jointapur, Sylhet, against Cherag Ali and 3 others (the purchasers/pre-emptee) and Haji Habibur Rahman is the seller-opposite party, while there are 9 others as the pro-forma opposite parties. The main contention of the petitioner is that 39 decimals of cultivable land, comprising the entire property of SA plot No. 169 of SA khatian No. 169, Mouza Thakurermati, PS Jointapur, District-Sylhet, fell into the shares of Shorbanu Bibi (the pro-forma opposite party No. 12), pursuant to the partition between her and other co-sharers. That Sarban Bibi, by a registered deed No. 8845 dated 21-8-1963, sold her entire 39 decimals of the suit property to Haji Habibur Rahman (seller)-opposite party No. 5. Thereafter, the said Haji Habibur Rahman has sold his entire 39 decimals of land lying at SA plot No. 169 to Cherag Ali and 3 others, vide sale deed No. 494 dated 3-3-1999 (Exhibit 2). Further contention of the petitioner is that, on 14-3-1999, he got to know, from some farmers, that the suit property has been purchased by the opposite party Nos. 1-4, from opposite party No. 5. Further case of the petitioner is that, he is the co-sharer in the SA khatian No. 169 of Mouza Thakurermati (Exhibit 1), but he was not informed by opposite party No. 1 about the intention to sell the suit property and no notice was given to him, under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. Therefore, he came to know about the sale of the property before 14-3-1999 and that he is a co-sharer of the suit property and the suit property is adjacent to his property and the suit property is needed to him.

4. The opposite party No. 1 (who is the next friend of opposite party No. 2-4) had filed written objection, on 4-1-2000, in which he has denied all material facts narrated in the miscellaneous petition for pre-emption and has stated his own case at paragraph No. 18 of the written objection. It has further been stated in the written objection that the petitioner Azizur Rahman resides at a different Mouza and that he is not a co-sharer in the suit property, nor he is a co-sharer of the Sarban Bibi, nor the property is adjacent to the property of the petitioner. His further contention is that the petitioner was aware of the fact of sale and he was a mediator in the sale process and that he had filed this pre-emption case only to harass him and the further case of the opposite party is that, there was no bonafide cause for filing this miscellaneous petition.

5. The pro-forma opposite party No. 9, Mollika Begum has also filed an application for transposition on 3-1-2000. The petitioner Azizur Rahman filed a written objection against the said application for transposition in which he has denied the allegation made in the petition for transposition and has stated that the opposite party No. 9 was residing from the far away from the suit property and that she has no property adjacent to the suit property and that one Ambor Ali, whose name has been recorded in SA khatian No. 169/1 who made an arrangement pursuant to which all the suit property was given to his two sons and no property of the said khatian was given to the opposite party No. 9 and he has also stated that, the suit property is adjacent to his property. After hearing, the said petition for transposition, the trial court has rejected the said application, vide it's order dated 16-5-2000. Against the said judgment and order dated 16-5-2000, the opposite party No. 9 had filed a petition, on 24-5-2000, for review of the said order, but that review petition was also dismissed by an order dated 30-5-2000 of the trial court. However, the opposite party No. 9 did not challenge the said order dated 30-5-2000 before any superior court. Rather this opposite party No. 9 had filed an appeal against the order dated 16-5-2000, which was numbered as Miscellaneous Appeal No. 43 of 2000, and the said appeal was allowed on 8-1-2002 and pursuant to order dated 8-1-2002, the opposite party No. 9 was transposed as co-petitioner, in the original Miscellaneous (Preemption) Case No. 12 of 1999.

6. The petitioner has examined himself as PW 1 and has also produced 2 witnesses, who were examined as PWs 2 and 3 to support of his case. The petitioner has also exhibited the SA khatian No. 169 as Exhibit 1, the transfer deed No. 494 dated 3-3-1999 (Exhibit 2). The co-petitioner Mollika Begum had examined herself as witness of the co-petitioner No. 2 to support her case and she had produced certain documents marked as Exhibit 3 and 4 series.

7. On the other hand, Asaddar Ali, father of the purchaser-opposite party Nos. 1-4 had testified as OPW No. 1 and deposed in support of the case of the opposite party No. 1-4. He deposed that, he had purchased the suit property in the names of his minor sons and it is his own property and the suit property is surrounded by his own property from 3 sides. Besides, the petitioner Azizur Rahman was present when the possession of the suit property was handed over.

8. The trial court, after hearing the parties, by it's judgment and order dated 20-2-2003 has allowed the pre-emption case No. 12 of 1999 and declared that the pre-emptor-petitioner as well as the transposed co-petitioner are entitled to purchase the suit property equally alongwith all rights and interest of the purchasers-opposite party Nos. 1-4 and had directed the co-petitioner/petitioner No. 2 to deposit the court fess within 45 (forty five) days.

9. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and order dated 20-2-2003, the petitioner Azizur Rahman preferred Miscellaneous (preemption) Appeal No. 43 of 2003, against co-petitioner Mollika Begum and others, on the ground that, the petitioner Azizur Rahman was entitled to purchase the entire suit property and that the trial court did not consider this aspect. On the other hand, the co-petitioner Mollika Begum/petitioner No. 2 preferred Miscellaneous (Pre-emption) Appeal No. 47 of 2003 claiming that she alone was entitled to purchase the entire suit property as the sole pre-emptor. Both the appeals were heard analogously by the Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Syhlet, who, by the impugned judgment and order 29-3-2007 has dismissed the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 43 of 2003, preferred by the petitioner Azizur Rahman, by setting aside the judgment and order of the trial court and allowed the Miscellaneous (Preemption) Appeal No. 47 of 2003, preferred by the co-petitioner/petitioner No. 2 Mollika Begum, thereby allowed her claim for preempting the entire suit property.

10. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgments and order dated 29-3-2007 of the appellate court, the petitioner Azizur Rahman has filed both these Civil Revision No. 3553 of 2007 and Civil Revision No. 3553 of 2007, under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and obtained both these Rules.

11. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that, the appellate court has failed to appreciate the legal aspect of this case in passing the impugned judgment and order by allowing the opposite party No. 9 Mollika Bibi absolute right of pre-emption. He also submits that, the impugned judgment and decree are totally misconceived and is contrary to the provisions of law and, in passing the impugned judgment and decree, the appellate court has committed grave error of law, resulting in error in the decision and occasioning failure of justice. Hence, the impugned judgments and decree are liable to be set-aside and the original petitioner No. 1 is entitled to get the 16 is suit property as the pre-emptor. The learned Advocate for the petitioner also submits that, after amendment of section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, in the year 2003, the court cannot grant any relief to the opposite parties Nos. 1 to 4, because they have not filed any of these revisional applications, nor they had preferred any appeal against the judgment and order dated 20-2-2003, passed by the trial court. He has prayed for making the Rule absolute on the grounds taken in the revisional applications. In the alternative, the learned Advocate prayed that the case may be remanded back for fresh trial.

12. Mrs. Syeda Rafika Khatun has opposed the Rules and submits that, the impugned order is based on proper appreciation of the facts and law. She also submits that there is no case of misreading or non-reading of evidence by the appellate court and in passing the impugned judgment and decree it has committed no error of law, nor the same has resulted in error in the decision occasioning any failure of justice. She concludes by submitting that, these Rules have no merit and these are liable to be discharged.

13. I have heard, the learned Advocate for both the parties/perused the revisional applications, the documents annexed thereto, the evidence and other materials on record.

14. Facts, for disposal of these Rules need not be repeated here.

15. It is evident from Exhibit No. 1, which is the SA Khatian No. 169 that, Sarban Bibi is a co-sharer in the said khatian alongwith Motwali of a Mosque Amir Mohammad, Ambor Ali and Azizur Rahman. The total property of the said khatian is 1.69 acres, lying at SA plot No. 169, 491, 600, 470, 462 and 177. It appears mat, the SA plot No. 169, which is the suit property, comprises 39 decimals of land and the nature of the suit property is cultivable land.

16. It is also admitted position that, the entire 39 decimals of land fell into the share of Sarban Bibi, through an amicable partition, amongst the co-sharers and that Sarban Bibi sold her 39 decimals of land, lying at SA plot No. 169, to Haji Habibur Rahman, vide registered deed No. 8845 dated 21-8-1963. Therefore, admittedly and evidently the said Haji Habibur Rahman was the absolute owner of 39 decimals of land of SA plot No. 169, since 21-8-1963 and the title and possession of Haji Habibur Rahman is not disputed by any party as well as it has been clearly proved by his chain of title and the evidence on record.

17. I also find that, this Haji Habibur Rahman has sold his entire 39 decimals of land, lying at SA plot No. 169, to Md Cherag Ali and 3 others, vide registered deed No. 494 dated 3-3-1999 and the sale is also admittedly the parties and the deed has been marked as Exhibit 2. Therefore, it is evident and proved that Sarban Bibi was one of the co-sharers in SA khatian No. 169 and that admittedly 39 decimals of land, lying at SA plot No. 169, fell into her share and she had sold the suit property to Haji Habibur Rahman, vide registered deed No. 8845 dated 21-8-1963. As such, Haji Habibur Rahman was owner of 39 decimals of land in SA Plot No. 169. Therefore, neither Ambor Ali nor Azizur Rahman was the co-sharers in the suit plot No. 169, in 39 decimals of land, since 21-8-1963. If the purchaser Haji Habibur Rahman had died at any time between 21-8-1963 to 3-3-1999, then neither Ambor Ali nor others would have been entitled to inherit this 39 decimals of land of SA Plot No. 169, sold by Haji Habibur Rahman on 3-3-1999 (Exhibit 2). Hence, Ambor Ali had no title in the suit property and he was not a co-sharer as heirs of Haji Habibur Rahman.

18. Therefore, the finding of the appellate court as recorded in the judgment passed by him that, “আম্বর আলীর মরনে তদীয় কন্যা ২নং সহ ছায়েল মল্লিকা বিবি এবং বিক্রেতা হাজী হাজী হাঁবিবুর রহমান নালিশী জমায় উত্তরাধিকারী সুত্রে সহ শরিকদার হয়” is totally perverse and contrary to the evidence on record, because Ambor Ali had no title in the suit property, while the seller Haji Habibur Rahman owned the suit property not as heir of Ambor Ali, but as purchaser, vide deed No. 8845 dated 21-8-1963.

19. The appellate court did not at all discuss about the admitted sale deed No. 8845 dated 21-8-1963, nor it's significance that had excluded the claim and right of both the plaintiffs, as heirs of Ambor Ali, to pre-empt the suit property. Besides, the appellate court has recorded that, “উভয় পক্ষে প্রদর্ত মৌখিক ও দলিলীক সাক্ষ্য পর্যালোচনায় ইহা দৃষ্ট হয় যে, বিক্রেতা তরফছানী হাজী হাবিবুর রহমান ২নং সহ ছায়েল মল্লিকা বিবি ভ্রাতা হয়। তাহাদের পিতার নাম আম্বর আলী । আম্বর আলী নালিশী জমায় রেক্ভীঁয় প্রজা হয় । আন্বর আলীর মরনে তদীয় কন্যা ২নং সহ ছায়েল মল্লিকা বিবি এবং বিক্রেতা হাজী হাবিবুর রহমান নালিশী জমায় উত্তরাধিকারী সূত্রে সহ শরিকদার হয়। পক্ষান্তরে, মূল ছায়েল আজিজুর রহমান নালিশী জমায় খরিদ সৃত্রে রেকর্ডীয়ি প্রজা হয়।” These findings are also totally perverse and tainted by misreading and non-reading of evidence on record, because Ambor Ali had no title in the suit property.

20. Admittedly, the suit property belonged to Sarban Bibi and she had sold her entire 39 decimals comprising the suit property, to Haji Habibur Rahman, vide deed No. 8845 dated 21-8-1963. Therefore, admittedly Ambor Ali had no title and he is not co-sharer in the suit property, in any manner. On the other hand, Ambor Ali was never a co-sharer, as has been rightly found by the trial court. The finding of the appellate court on this issue is totally an outcome of misreading and non-reading of the evidence on record, while that of the trial court, on this issue, is correct.

21. I also find that, the appellate court, very surprisingly, had made a 3rd case that the petitioner Azizur -Rahman has purchased the suit property.

22. Therefore, the concurrent findings of the courts below are liable to be reversed and set-aside, save the finding of the trial that Ambor Ali was not a co-sharer in the suit property.

23. On the other hand, it is to be recorded here that, the opposite party No. 9 has applied for transposition of her name as co-petitioner, vide application dated 3-1-2000 and the original petitioner Azizur Rahman had vehemently opposed the same by filing a written objection against the application for transposition. As such, the interest of the original petitioner Azizur Rahman was in conflict with that of the opposite party No. 9.

24. It is a settled law that, in a case, where the case and interest of the defendant is in conflict with that of the plaintiff, the prayer for transposition as co-plaintiff or as co-petitioner cannot be allowed. This position of law has already been settled by this Court in several decisions. Transposition is allowed only if the defendant (or the opposite party) admits the case of the plaintiff (or the petitioner) and, therefore, transposition. Because, obviously, the transposed defendant can neither give evidence beyond the pleadings of the plaintiff, nor can amend the same by contradicting the case stated by the plaintiff or by amending the same by intruding a different case.

25. Besides, the trial court had rejected the petition for transposition by it's order dated 16-5-2000 and the opposite party No. 9 had also filed a petition for review of the said order and the review petition was rejected on 30-4-2001 by the trial court. This order was appealable order, but the opposite party No. 9 did not prefer any appeal against the order dated 30-4-2001, rather she had filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 43 of 2000, against the order dated 16-5-2000, and the said appeal was allowed on 8-1-2001 and pursuant to the said order dated 8-1-2001, she was transposes as co-petitioner. Therefore, this order dated 8-1-2001 was tenable in view of the order dated 30-4-2001 which was not challenged and, therefore, had became final and binding on her.

26. When at any stage, this kind of illegality has come to the notice of the court, the court has ample jurisdiction to set-aside the said unlawful order dated 8-1-2001, passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 43 of 2000, because this Court cannot perpetuate an illegality when it has come to it's notice and the court can correct it in exercise of the power vested in it under Article 109 of the Constitution of the Peoples Republic of Bangladesh read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

27. Besides, the right of pre-emption of the petitioner No. 2 (transposed plaintiff) was barred by limitation, since long after expiry of 4 months period of statutory limitation, this petition for transposition was allowed though wrongly. Provisions of section 22(1) of the Limitation Act, 1908, is applicable in this circumstance. Section 22(1) reads as follows:
"22. Effect of substituting or adding new plaintiff or defendant-(1) Where, after the institution of a suit, a new plaintiff or defendant is substituted or added, the suit shall, as regards him, be deemed to have been instituted when he was so made a party."

28. Therefore, as per provisions of section 22(1) of the Limitation Act, 1908, so far as the petitioner No. 2 is concerned, the pre-emption case shall be deemed to have been filed on 8-1-2001 i.e. when she has been added as co-plaintiff, by way of transposition. Hence, her claim for pre-emption was hopelessly barred by limitation.

29. This case is a glaring instance of injustice to the minors, who were opposite party Nos. 2-4, the entire suit property, lying at plot No. 169, was purchased by the father of these minors, from the person who had been owing the suit property since 1963. The opposite party Nos. 2-4 are not present before this court. However, the court is bound to decide the matter on merit, even if, one of the party is not present. Absence of a party does not discharge the plaintiff from their case, nor will minimize their burden.

30. The provisions of section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, as it stands today, stipulates as to who may file an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. It provides that, on the application of any party a proceeding under section 115(1) can be initiated. In other words, a third party cannot file a revisional application as per the amended provisions of section 115(1) or 115(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. Admittedly, both these proceedings have been initiated by Azizur Rahman, who is a party to the proceedings. Therefore, initiation of this proceeding is lawful. Now, a lawful proceeding may be allowed or dismissed on merit as well as this Court "may revise such decree or order and make such order, in the suit or proceedings, as it thinks fit", vide the provisions of sub-section (1) and (2) of section 115 of the Code.

31. Since, in a lawfully initiated proceedings this Court has ample jurisdiction to revise the impugned order as it is authorized to pass such order as it thinks fit. It is, therefore, immaterial whether or not the opposite party Nos. 1-4 have or have not filed these revisional applications.

32. Besides, the evidences on record are adequate to adjudicate all the issues involved in these two matters. Hence/there is no reason to send the case on remand for a fresh trial or hearing.

33. In view of the forgoing discussions and the provisions of law, I find no merit in, these 2(two) Rules, which are liable to be discharged.

34. In the result, both these Rules, issued in Civil Revision No. 3554 of 2007 and Civil Revision No. 3553 of 2007, are hereby discharged.

35. The impugned judgment and order dated 29-3-2007, passed by the Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet, in Miscellaneous Appeal (Pre-emption) No. 47 of 2003 (Heard analogously with Miscellaneous Appeal No. 43 of 2003), dismissing the appeal and thereby reversing the judgment and order dated 20-2-2003, passed by the Assistant Judge, Jointapur, Sylhet, in Miscellaneous (Preemption) Case No. 12 of 1999, are hereby set-aside.

36. The Miscellaneous Pre-emption Case No. 12 of 1999 is hereby dismissed. Consequently, both the Miscellaneous (Preemption) Appeal Nos. 43 of 2003 and 47 of 2003 shall stand dismissed.

37. The original opposite party Nos. 1-4 (purchasers) are entitled to own, posses and enjoy the 16 annas of the suit property as the purchasers.

A decree shall be drawn accordingly.

The order of stay granted earlier by this Court is hereby vacated.

No costs.
Let a copy of this judgment be sent down to the concerned Courts at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Fatema Najib J: 1. This appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 23.09.2012 passed by learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Noakhali in Title Suit No.72 of 2007 decreed the suit in part.
2. One Arati Bala Dey as sole plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.72 of 2007 on 04.11.2007 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Noakhali impleading the appellants as defendant nos. 1 and 2 and the respondent nos. 3-21 as defendant nos.3-14 praying for partition of 2.33 2/3 decimals of land more fully described in the schedule to the plaint. During pendency of the suit, sole plaintiff, Arati Bala Dey died and her daughter who was originally impleaded as defendant no.14, her name has been struck off from defendant by Order no.7 dated 28.04.2008 and substituted her as plaintiff no. 1(ka) in place of Arati Bala Dey. Subsequently, defendant no.6 died and his heirs has been duly substituted as defendant nos.16-19 vide order no. 20 dated 17.02.2009. Sheema Rani Dey, Jarna daughter of Robindra Kumar Dey, who converted to Muslim was added as defendant no. 15 in the name of Jannatul Ferdous vide order no.20 dated 17.02.2009. Polash Chandra Pal, son of Mira Rani Dey and Sujun Chandra Pal son of Ira Rani Dey have been substituted as plaintiffs vide order No.73 dated 11.09.2012. On the prayer of the plaintiff the defendant nos. 20-21 was added as defendants. In the appeal the respondent nos. 5-8 died and since they did not contest the suit, their heirs were not substituted and their names have been struck off from the memo of appeal by order dated 06.05.2014.
3. The case of the plaintiff, in brief, is that, the suit land measuring 5.10 decimals of land was originally belonged to Rabindra Kumar Dey, who got the same through gift and inheritance from his mother and father respectively. After transferring, while possessing 4.81 decimals of land, Rabindra Kumar Dey died leaving behind wife Arati Bala Dey, two sons namely, Prodip Kumar Dey and Probir Kumar Dey and four daughters Mira Bali Dey, Ira Rani Dey, Sheema Rani Dey and Shipra Rani Dey. Mira Rani Dey and Ira Rani Dey got married during life time of their father and the rest two daughters and two sons were minors at the time of death of their father Rabindra Kumar Dey. According to Daya Bagha School unmarried daughters can enjoy the land of their father till marriage. Arati Bala Dey while owning and possessing the suit land with her two sons, Prodip Kumar Dey, died leaving behind mother and brother Probir, who converted to Muslim. Sheema Rani Dey, daughter of Rabindra Kumar Dey, also converted to Muslim and married a Muslim boy. The plaintiff Arati Bala Dey got 13 i.e. 1.60 13 decimals out of total land 4.81 decimals of land by inheritance from her husband. Prodip Kumar Dey out of his share 1.60 1/3 decimals of land sold way 0.27 decimal during his life time. So, the plaintiff Arati Bala Dey got 1.60 1/3 decimals by inheritance from her husband and son Prodip had 1.33 1/3 decimals after selling 0.27decimals of land. In this way Arati Bala Dey and Prodip Kumer Dey got together 2.93 1/3 decimals of land. The plaintiff Arati Bala Dey along with her unmarried daughter Sipra Rani Dey, who later on was substituted as plaintiff no. 1 (ka) in place of Arati Bala Dey had been living in a house situated at S. A. plot no.921 of S. A. Khatian No.253. The plaintiff Arati Bala Dey claimed partition which the defendant no.1 Probir Kumar Dey denied the same on 25.09.2007. So, the plaintiff, Arati Bala Dey was constrained to file the present suit.
4. The defendant no.1, Probir Kumar Dey alias Saiful Islam contested the suit by filing a written statement contending, interalia, that the suit land was belonged to his father, Rabindra Kumar Dey, who died on 05.10.1978 leaving behind two sons namely, Probir Kumar Dey and Prodip Kumar Dey, wife, the plaintiff Arati Bala Dey and four daughters. But according to Daya Bagha School the wife and daughters of Rabindra Kumar Dey are not entitled to get saham in the suit land. Prodip sold out his entire shares to different persons and extinguished title in the suit land; that the plaintiff earlier filed Title Suit No. 11 of 1990 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Chatkhil for the same land and in the plaint she admitted that Prodip sold his entire share and Prodip and Probir inherited the land of their late father Rabindra Kumar Dey in equal shares measuring 2.40 1/2 acres; that the aforesaid suit was filed by mother of Probir, Arati Bala Dey as legal guardian of her minor son, Probir and suit was decreed on 20.06.1992; that against the said decree Abdul Khaleque filed Title Appeal No.34 of 1990 in the Court of District Judge, Noakhali, which was dismissed on 23.07.1991 and the decree passed by the trial court was affirmed; that this defendant Probir as youngest son of Rabindra Kumar Dey inherited his 2.40 1/2 acres in the suit khatian and has been possessing the same. The further case of the defendant is that Sheema Rani Dey, daughter of Rabindra Kumar Dey also converted to Muslim and married a Muslim man. The plaintiff Arati Bala Dey died and her unmarried daughter Shipra Rani Dey was substituted as plaintiff in the suit in her place but substituted plaintiff is not legally entitled to get any saham in the present suit. Further case of the defendant is that he embraced Islam religion voluntarily on 05.07.1999 and changed his name Md. Saiful Islam, married Rojina Akhter on 30.09.1999 and living in his Paternal house with family situated in khatian No.253, Plot no.121; that although present B. S. D. P. Khatian No.350 was recorded in his name for 01.64 acres of land but he has been in possession of 2.40 1/2 acres; that on the other hand, since he is not the owner of the suit khatian, his name was not recorded in the present khatian; that as per Hindu law, when a son acquired property by inheritance from his father and latter changed religion, he will not be deprived from his father’s property. Thus there is no legal bar for defendant no.1 for getting saham in the property left by his deceased father, Rabindra Kumar Dey. With these averments, the defendant no. 1 prayed for dismissal of the suit and claimed saham of 2.40 1/2 acres in the suit khatians.
5. The defendant nos. 2 and 21 contested the suit by filing separate written statement. The defendant no.2 Rustom Ali claimed saham in 0.36 acres by way of registered Ewaz Deed No.6119 dated 23.11.2010 with the defendant no.1. The Added-defendant no. 21, Abdul Malek claimed 0.41 decimals of land in suit plot no.121 by purchases from Prodip Kumar Dey and defendant no.1.
6. The trial court framed the following issues:
1. Whether the plaintiff Arati Bala Dey inherited from her deceased husband Rabindra Kumar Dey?
2. Whether the substituted plaintiff Sipra Rani Dey is entitled to inherit of her deceased father and mother?
3. Whether the plaintiffs are entitled to a decree for partition as prayed for?
7. In the suit the plaintiff examined only one witness as P.W-1 and the documents produced which were marked as Exhibits 1 and 2. On the other hand, the defendant no.1 examined only one witness as D.W.1 and produced the documents which were marked as Exhibits Ka-Jha. The defendant nos. 2 and 21 did not produce any oral or documentary evidence.
8. The trial court after considering the oral and documentary evidences produced by the parties decreed the suit in part for 1.60 13 acres land on contest in preliminary form against the defendant no.1 and ex-parte against other defendants without cost by judgment and decree dated 23.04.2012.
9. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree dated 23.04.2012 the defendant no.1, Probir Kumar Dey preferred this appeal.
10. Mr. N. K. Shaha, the learned Advocate on behalf of the defendant nos.1 and 2 appellants submits that Hindu widow can not inherit the property of her husband since the widow gets only life time interest. He further submits that intestate succession the property of male and female Hindus is governed by the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 and same is applicable in the present suit. He next submits that the defendant no.1 converted to Muslim from Hindu after death of his father and such conversion is no ground for exclusion of inheritance under Section 23 and 26 of the said Act. In this respect reference was made to the decision reported in (1911) ILR 33, Allahabad 356. He also submits that Arati Bala Dey earlier filed a suit wherein in the plaint it was stated that Probir and Prodip got 8(eight) annas each of the property of Rabindra Kumar Dey. So, Arati Bala Dey can not claim share of Rabindra Kumer Dey. He finally submits that Arati Bala Dey and after her death Sipra Rani Dey can not inherit the property of Rabindra Kumar Dey.
11. Mr. Tusher Kanti Roy, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-respondent submits that the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 was enacted on 17.06.1956 in India and as such the provisions of the said Act have no manner of application in Bangladesh. He further submits the inheritance of Hindu women is governed by Hindu Women’s Rights to Property Act, (XVIII of 1937) which is still in force in Bangladesh and not repealed by the Bangladesh Laws (Revision and Declaration) Act, 1973 as specified in the First Schedule under Article 2 of the Act, 1973 and will be applicable in the present suit. He by referring section 3(1) of the said Act submits that Rabindra Kumar Dey died on 5.10.1978 and his wife Arati Bala Dey entitled in respect of the property to the same share as of son. He next submits that Arati Bala Dey as widow can file a partition suit. After death of Arati Bala Dey on 24.08.2008 the property which she inherited from her husband Rabindra Kumar Dey the same will be inherited by the next heir of the person from whom she inherited. The only son Probir Kumer Dey, defendant no. 1 was alive at the time of death of Arati Bala Dey but since the defendant no.1 converted to Muslim in the year 1999 and same is a ground of forfeiture of property and exclusion from inheritance as the son had changed his religion. He finally submits the substituted plaintiff, Sipra Rani Dey, the unmarried daughter of deceased Rabindra Kumar Dey as next heir is entitled to inherit the property and as such Shipra Rani Dey rightly got 1.60 1/3 decimals of land and there is no illegality in passing the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned Joint District Judge.
12. Heard the learned lawyers of respective parties. Perused the oral and documentary evidences and materials on record and the relevant provisions of the Hindu law.
13. Admittedly, the suit property measuring an area of 4.81 decimals belonged to Rabindra Kumar Dey and he died on 05.10.1978 leaving behind wife Arati Bala Dey, two sons namely, Probir Kumar Dey, defendant no.1 and Prodip Kumar Dey and four daughters namely, Mira Bala Dey, Ira Rani Dey, Sheema Rani Dey and Sipra Rani Dey. Prodip died leaving behind mother, Arati Bala Dey, brother Probir and four sisters. Probir converted to Muslim from Hindu in the year 1999. Among four daughters three daughters namely, Mira Bala Dey, Ira Rani Dey, Sheema Rani Dey were married and also converted to Muslim.
14. The positive case of the plaintiff is that after death of Rabindra Kumar Dey, Arati Bala Dey inherited the same share as a son in respect of property of Rabindra Kumer Dey. In this way she inherited 1/3 share i.e. 1.60 1/3 decimal out of total 4.81 decimals of land. After death of Arati Bala Dey on 24.08.2008, the property was passed to the next heir Shipra Rani Dey, unmarried daughter of Rabindra Kumar Dey. The further assertion of the plaintiff is that at the time of death of Arati Bala Day, one son Probir, the defendant no.1, one unmarried daughter Shipra Rani Dey and other married daughters were alive. But son Probir converted to Muslim in the year 1999 and thereby excluded to inherit the property of Rabindra Kumar Dey after conversion. Further according to Hindu law unmarried daughter, Shipra Rani Dey will inherit the same as next heir of Rabindra Kumar Dey from whom Arati Bala Dey got it for her life time interest.
15.The defendant no-1 mainly contended that Arati Bala or after her death the unmarried daughter Shipra Rani Dey did not inherit the property of Rabindra Kumer Dey as per Hindu Succession Act, 1956. Though Probir became a Muslim, he did not forfeit his interest and exclusion from inheritance from the property of his deceased father, Rabindra Kumer Dey by reason of his conversion to Muslim.
16.The learned Advocate for the defendant no.1 by referring the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 submits that Arati Bala Dey as widow or after her death unmarried daughter Shipra Rani Dey is not entitled to inherit the property left by Rabindra Kumer Dey. We have carefully examined the Hindu Succession Act, 1956. The aforesaid Act was enacted on 17.06.1956 by parliament in the seventh year of the Republic of India. No where in this Act it was stated that it extends to the whole of Pakistan and after libration the word ‘Bangladesh’ was substituted and as such the provisions of the said Act has no manner of application in the present case. In support of this he relied on the decision of the Privy Council in the case of Gobind Krishna Narain and another versus Khunni Lal reported in (1911) ILR 33 Allahabad 35. The cited case decided on a different state of facts, law and were distinguishable from the present case. In our opinion, this decision does not support the contention of Mr. N.K. Shaha.
17. In paragraph no. 6 (ka) of the written statement filed by the defendant no.1 it was stated that Arati Bala Dey on behalf of her minor son Probir Kumar Dey, the defendant no.1 herein filed Title Suit No. 11 of 1990 for permanent injunction and in the plaint it was stated that Probir Kumar Dey and Prodip Kumer Dey got 2.40 1/2 decimals of land each left by their deceased father. That suit was decreed and also upheld in appeal. But now the learned Advocate of the defendant no.1 submits Arati Bala Dey can not claim that she will get a saham by inheritance on the property left by Rabindra Kumer Dey. On perusal Exhibit Um- Um (2) series it appears that the said suit was filed for permanent injunction filed by Arathi Bala Dey on behalf of his minor son Probir Kumer Dey and same was decreed ex-parte. There is no evidence on record to show that any appeal was filed against the said ex-parte decree or the said ex-parte decree was set aside. Since the issues, subject matter and the parties of the said suit are not same, we find there is no legal bar for Arati Bala Dey to claim a saham in the property left by her husband and legally entitled to file the present suit for partition.
18. Let us now consider whether a Hindu widow is entitled to get the same share as a son. In this connection reference may be made to section 3 of the Hindu Women’s Rights to Property Act, 1937 (XVIII of 1937). Sub section (1) of section 3 of the said Act says that when a Hindu governed by the Daya Bagha School of Hindu Law dies intestate leaving any property dies, his widow, shall, subject to the provisions of sub-section(3), be entitled to the same share as a sons. Sub-section (3) of section 3 of the said Act further says that any interest devolving on a Hindu widow shall be the limited interest known as a Hindu Woman’s estate, but she shall have the same right of claiming partition as a male owner. Further sub-section (2) of section 1 of the said Act stipulates that it extends to the whole of Bangladesh.
19. Thus from reading of the aforesaid provisions of sub-sections (1) and (3) of the Hindu Women’s Rights to Property Act, 1937 it is clear that the widow during the period of her life time she became complete owner and co-sharer of the property and this sub-section 3(3) has the effect of putting the widow in the same position as a son in the matter of claiming partition and consequently having the right to claim partition filed the present suit. Thus Arati Bala Dey as heirs of Rabindra Kumar Dey shall get 1/3 rd share = 1.60 1/3 decimals out of total 4.81 decimals.
20. The plaintiff alleged that Prodip Kumar Dey died unmarried leaving behind Arati Bala Dey as heir and since Probir by this time change religion converted to Muslim and exclusion of inheritance from the property of his deceased father. The contesting defendant no.1 alleged that Prodip sold out his shares during his life time. The learned trial court in its judgment found that Prodip sold out his shares to different people and nothing was remained. The defendants did not file appeal or cross objection against those findings. So, the defendants can not raise this issue in the present appeal.
21. Now, the question may arise whether the substituted-plaintiff Shipra Rani, unmarried daughter of Rabindra Kumar Dey is entitled to inherit the property of Arati Bala Dey which Arati Bala got for life time interest from her husband, Rabindra Kumar Dey.
<u>22. In Commentaries 168(4) of Mulla’s Principles of Hindu law speaks every female whether she is a widow, who succeeds as heirs to the property of male, takes only a limited estate in the property inherited by her, and at her death the property passes not to her heir, but to the next heir of the male from whom she inherited it. So, after the death of Arati Bala, her inherited property will pass to the next heirs of original owner Rabindra Kumar Dey. At the time of death of Arati Bala Rabindra Kumar Dey had one son, defendant no.1, one unmarried daughter i.e. the plaintiff Sipra Rani Dey and other three married daughters. Admittedly, son Probir Kumar Dey, defendant no.1 converted to Muslim in the year 1999. Hindu law does not apply where a person enters into a religious order renouncing all worldly affairs, his action is tantamount to Civil death, and it excludes him altogether from inheritance and from a share on partition. So, conversion from the Hindu to the Mahomedan faith by the defendant no.1 Probir debarred him from inheriting the property of his father at the time of opening the inheritance on 24.08.2008 when Arati Bala Dey died. It is pertinent to note that Hindu law is religious law, the right to property is made by that law dependent upon the observance of the tenants of that faith. Consequently, a lapse from orthodox practices of Hinduism would under that law entail forfeiture of the caste and all rights to property and inheritance. Renouncement of religion has a disability, but after the passing of the Caste Disability Removal Act, 1850 (Act XXI of 1950), change of religion is no ground of exclusion of inheritance. But after the repealing of the Act XXI of 1850 by the Bangladesh Laws (Revision and Declaration Act, 1973 (Act No. VIII of 1973) the persons converts into another religion are now forfeited from the inheritance and from the joint family property and fathers property. It will not be out of place to mention that when a Hindu adopting by the Mahomedan faith, from the moment of this conversion, by that acts affects all the property he acquires subsequently to it, so to render it subject to be Muslim law of inheritance. Commentaries 43(5) of the aforesaid Book states As between daughters the inheritance goes, first, to the unmarried daughters. As already observed above, Shipra Rani Dey was only unmarried daughter of Rabindra Kumar Dey, who was alive at the time of death of Arati Bala Dey on 24.08.2008. So, Sipra Rani Dey as the only unmarried daughter of Rabindra Kumar Dey will get 1.60 1/3 decimals of land which was passed to Rabindra Kumar Dey due to demise of his wife, Arati Bala Dey.</u>
23. It is pertinent to mentioned that Probir, son of Rabindra Kumar Dey got 1/3 of 4.81 i.e. 1.60 1/3 decimals of land at the death of Rabindra Kumar Dey on 05.10.1978 when he was Hindu. The defendant no.1 also filed an application for saham and paid court fee on 27.08.2012 which was kept with the record. So, the defendant no.1 will get a saham for 1.60 1/3 decimals of land and not 2.40 12 acres as claimed by him in the present suit.
24. It appears from the record that as per judgment and decree the plaintiff prayed for commission to make partition in respect of her shares allotted by court on 04.11.2012. Accordingly, Advocate Commissioner was appointed and after Commission learned Advocate Commissioner submitted his report. Subsequently, all proceedings of the suit was stayed since the present appeal was filed against the impugned judgment and decree dated 23.09.2012.
25. Having regard to facts and circumstances, we are of the view that trial court on proper consideration and appreciation of the evidence and materials on record rightly decreed the suit in part on finding that the original plaintiff, Arati Rani Bala Dey wife of Rabindra Kumar Dey became owner and co-sharer of the property and had right to file the suit for partition during her life time. After her death, her share was passed to Rabindra Kumar Dey from whom she inherited and Shipra Rani Dey as only unmarried daughter of Rabindra Kumar Dey will get the same from Rabindra Kumar Dey as next heir since the only son Probir Kumar Dey, who was alive but converted to Muslim earlier before opening the inheritance of Rabindra Kumar Dey on the property which was passed from Arati Bala Dey at her death on 24.04.2008.
26. Thus we find no merit in this appeal.
27. In the result, the appeal is dismissed and the impugned judgment and decree dated 23.09.2012 is affirmed.
28. Send down the lower court records along with a copy of this judgment at once.
End.
